title: 1f512 reading line
description: One append-only JSONL row from the falsifiability registry. A stranger with an RPC recomputes the verdict from the published exchanges; the row is hash-chained so a removed or reordered line breaks every successor. Soft-power: a schema that only encodes HELD is not a schema for this project — UNREADABLE and DEFAULTED are first-class verdicts, not error paths. Provider values are labels, never URLs (RPC paths carry keys; this log is public and append-only).

commitment.description: Id of the commitment this reading is about.

verdict.description: Closed four-verdict set. A format that drops UNREADABLE or DEFAULTED pushes failure into prose where nothing can check it.

reason.description: Machine-branchable why. Prose belongs in note.

rpc.description: Every exchange that produced this verdict. HELD/BROKEN/DEFAULTED require two agreeing providers (minItems 2). UNREADABLE may carry zero, one, or two — a failed attempt is evidence, not something to invent an exchange for.

read_at.description: When the reading was taken, ms since epoch, UTC. Not Date.now() inside pure evaluate — the caller supplies T.

note.description: Optional human prose (provider error text, operator context). Never a substitute for reason.

prev_hash.description: Hash of the previous line, or empty string for the first. Chaining on the recomputed hash, not the claimed one.

hash.description: sha256 hex over the canonical preimage of content + prev_hash.

sig.description: Optional signature over hash, base64url. Proves who wrote, never that what they wrote is true.

key.description: Optional key id that produced sig.

provider.description: Stable label for the endpoint, NEVER its URL. A URL-shaped value is a published API key waiting to happen.

params.description: RPC params as sent. A stranger re-asks with these.

result.description: Response as received. This is what a stranger re-derives the verdict from.

at_block.description: Block height the answer was pinned to.
